new_statements.quote: [pp.120-121] 5.3 Sistem Morfologi. a. Kebanyakan kata dasar bahasa Melayu Bangka terdiri dari dua suku kata dengan tekanan primer pada suku kata kedua dari belakang. [pp.50-51] Bahasa Melayu Bangka dengan sendirinya mempunyai nada, tekanan, dan panjang. Akan tetapi, ketiganya tidak dapat dikatakan fonem dalam bahasa ini. Ciri utama fonem adalah kemampuannya membedakan arti, sedangkan di dalam Bahasa Melayu Bangka, nada, tekanan, dan panjangnya ujaran kata tidak membedakan arti kata. Dalam ujaran yang lebih besar daripada kata, misalnya frase atau kalimat, nada, tekanan, dan panjang ujaran dapat mengubah arti.
new_statements.translation: [pp.120-121] 5.3 Morphological system. a. Most base words of Bangka Malay consist of two syllables, with primary stress on the second syllable from the end. [pp.50-51] Bangka Malay naturally has pitch, stress and length. However, none of the three can be called a phoneme in this language. The main property of a phoneme is its ability to distinguish meaning, whereas in Bangka Malay the pitch, stress and length of a word utterance do not distinguish word meaning. In utterances larger than the word, e.g. phrase or sentence, pitch, stress and length can change meaning.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive; primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (typically disyllabic) base word.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said (only 'tekanan primer' is mentioned, implying but not describing secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: None. No statement about schwa penults or about stress under suffixation; the rule is stated for kata dasar (base words) only.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for base words (kata dasar) in the concluding summary; sec. 2.5 adds that stress/pitch/length are meaningful only at phrase/sentence level (intonation), treated under syntax. Data mainly from the Bangka Tengah dialect (Pangkalpinang/Sungailiat).
new_statements.identity_note: Mustafa et al. 1984 describe 'bahasa Melayu Bangka' of Kabupaten Bangka and Kotamadya Pangkalpinang (then South Sumatra province); they list five dialects (Bangka Barat/Mentok, Utara, Selatan, Tengah, Cina) and state the sample was centred on Melayu Bangka Tengah (Pangkalpinang, Sungailiat, Mendo Barat). This is Glottolog bang1365 Bangka [mfb]; the Lom/Mapur variety (separate Glottolog entry) is mentioned but not described. McDowell & Anderbeck 2020, named by the earlier scan, explicitly excludes Bangka and Belitung and is not a source for this language.

sources.note: Sec. 2.5 Fonem Suprasegmental (pp.50-51): pitch, stress and length exist but are not phonemic at word level ('tidak membedakan arti kata'); only juncture is phonemic. Bab V Kesimpulan 5.3a (pp.120-121): most base words are disyllabic with primary stress on the penultimate syllable. Verified on page images (PDF pp.68, 137-138).
